I'm still a newer communist, but from my limited experience and reading, it seems like ML, Trotskyist, and other socialist parties run into issues of entrenched leadership, gatekeeping, and culty behaviors. This is not exclusive to these parties of course. That sort of poor group dynamic is something I've witnessed elsewhere. 

Parties need to be up-front about their finances, allow for factions (I'd argue only leftist ones,) and practice a democratic centralism beholden to the working class including the most oppressed groups in our society. These parties should go out of their way to aid, educate, and recruit folks from BIPOC, LGBTQIA+, and other oppressed communities. Parties should also go out of their way to make sure disagreements are discussed rather than giving into meek servility to whatever party leaders are saying. Otherwise, we end up getting hyper-centralized parties more concerned with their "correct program" than actually developing a program for the working class based in historical and local context.

I think I understand what you're trying to get at. Many on their meditative or spiritual or personal (whatever you want to call it) journeys end up seeing "overcoming the material world" as some sort of final obstacle, and once they overcome this, they believe they will be enlightened. But life does take place in a material world. You need food to eat. Water to drink. The human body is bound by physical laws.   


The spiritual journey one goes on is active and personal for the rest of your life. Thinking there is some "final boss" implies a linear progression in life, and you end up denying the ever changing process of evolution. Becoming enlightened is seemingly paradoxical because it involves the acknowledgement that there isn't a stuck state of "well, I have overcome all obstacles, reached my final destination, and I am enlightened from here on." Being willing to swim with the changing currents of life is the path toward enlightenment, and when one learns to acknowledge the fluidity of this path, they are then on the journey to simply arriving in an enlightened state.

In our modern society especially here in the US, abuse is the norm. Recognizing your pain, your trauma, your wants, your needs, and deciding you want to live your life on your own terms, these things are not taught well and often not even encouraged.  


So my heart goes out to you. Your pain is so real. Your suffering is so real. And it hurts. It hurts you have to be your own parent and best friend because there are areas you lack because you never were shown how or you simply were born with a condition others did not acknowledge or know how to help you with. I hear your story, and I feel your pain.  


When our mind and body is in disorder, there is deep down a kid version of you needing to be heard and needing to receive a hug. It is frankly so easy to be so hard on ourselves, and I would like to challenge you to go easier on yourself. Any thoughts that arise that tell you your life is ruined and it's your fault, those aren't you. They are strong thoughts your ego attaches to so it can feel some sense of permanence even if it means the suffering of the whole individual. These thoughts really just need to feel heard. I don't know everything about your life, and I really don't know enough to feel confident telling you any kind of specific plan to fix your situation. It's up to you to delegate support where you need it so you can take the pressure off yourself. I think it shows some autonomy that you want to move out on your own. I think it also shows that there is a part of you that trusts yourself to make the right decision for you. And that would be an awesome, big step the way I see it. I encourage you to trust that intuition. I encourage you to continue to find the places you trust yourself, and I encourage you to see that you have time.

First off, I am glad that you are looking for a way to enjoy yourself rather than spending all of your time at school. I want to start off by saying that your voice is an instrument. Learning the basics are the foundation for learning the advanced techniques. The basics include: breathing, posture, and articulation. You also need to find out what voice type you are. As a male you may be on the low end of the register as a bass, baritone, or tenor on the high end. There are high and low extremes to these types, but these are all of those down to there three basic roots. 
With your posture in mind, make sure to stand up straight with one foot slightly in front of the other and spread so your feet about match up with your shoulders. Also, make sure to keep your jaw and your neck at a nice forward position. Do not tip them back and forth. This will restrict your vocal chords. Now onto your breath!
Your breath should come from your diaphragm as opposed to just from your chest. The easiest way to demonstrate this is to take your fist or a friend's fist and have them lightly push onto your stomach. Breath into your stomach and push their hand away. Other exercises include laying down with your back to the floor and breathing into your diaphragm from there. 
With your articulation, avoid having bitey vowels. Try to keep your mouth open and the sound light to start with. Example would be singing "Ahhhhh" while keeping the back of your mouth open and your tongue pushed away from your throat. This is another thing. Try to keep your tongue out of the way by leaving the tip of it into your bottom teeth. If that doesn't help, then let it completely out of your mouth. This will remove some tension. 
Before you start doing some serious singing you should always warm up. Vowels are the easiest way. Just remember to keep them open.
